facts.title: A Caterpillar Digests Itself Into Soup Before It Becomes a Butterfly
facts.summary: Inside a chrysalis, a caterpillar does not simply sprout wings.

facts.title: Butterflies First Appeared in the Americas About 100 Million Years Ago
facts.summary: Butterflies most likely originated in western North America or Central America about 100 million years ago, not in Asia, as many scientists had long assumed.

facts.title: California's Wintering Monarchs Fell From Millions to Under 2,000 in 2020
facts.summary: In the winter of 2020, volunteers counted fewer than 2,000 western monarch butterflies at their overwintering sites on the California coast, a drop of more than 99.9% since the 1980s.

facts.title: Four in Five UK Butterfly Species Have Declined Since the 1970s
facts.summary: About four out of five butterfly species in the United Kingdom have declined since the 1970s, according to the State of the UK's Butterflies 2022 report by the charity Butterfly Conservation, published in February 2023.

facts.title: Large Blue Caterpillars Live 10 Months Inside Ant Nests, Eating the Ants' Young
facts.summary: The large blue butterfly spends about 10 months of its life inside a red ant nest, where the ants look after it as if it were one of their own while it eats their young.

facts.title: Monarch Butterflies Born in Late Summer Live Eight Times Longer Than Their Parents
facts.summary: The last monarch butterflies born each summer in North America belong to a "super generation" that can live up to eight months, about eight times longer than their parents and grandparents.

facts.title: Monarch Butterflies Keep Time for Their Sun Compass in Their Antennae
facts.summary: Migrating monarch butterflies steer by the sun, and the clock that corrects for the sun's movement across the sky sits in their antennae, not only in their brains.

facts.title: Painted Lady Butterflies Cross the Sahara on a 12,000-Kilometer Yearly Round Trip
facts.summary: Painted lady butterflies make an annual round trip of about 12,000 kilometers between Europe and tropical Africa, crossing the Sahara Desert in both directions.

facts.title: Pollen-Eating Heliconius Butterflies Can Live for Nearly a Year
facts.summary: Heliconius butterflies live about three times longer than their close relatives, often surviving several months in the wild, and one species, Heliconius hewitsoni, was recorded living up to 348 days in captivity.

facts.title: San Francisco's Growth Wiped Out the Xerces Blue Butterfly by the 1940s
facts.summary: The Xerces blue, a small butterfly of San Francisco's coastal sand dunes, is considered one of the first butterflies in the United States lost to human impact.

facts.title: The Blue Morpho's Dazzling Blue Wings Contain No Blue Pigment
facts.summary: The brilliant blue of a blue morpho butterfly's wings contains no blue pigment at all.

facts.title: The Common Bluebottle Butterfly Has 15 Kinds of Light Sensors in Its Eyes
facts.summary: The common bluebottle, a swallowtail butterfly of Australasia, has at least 15 classes of photoreceptors in its eyes.

facts.title: The Glasswing Butterfly's Wings Reflect Less Light Than a Pane of Glass
facts.summary: The clear patches on the wings of the glasswing butterfly, Greta oto, reflect only about 2 to 5 percent of light, depending on the viewing angle, which makes the insect hard for predators to spot.

facts.title: The Viceroy Butterfly Is Not Just a Harmless Copycat of a Toxic Species
facts.summary: The viceroy butterfly, long taught as the textbook example of a harmless insect copying a foul-tasting one, can itself be distasteful to predators.

facts.title: The World's Largest Butterfly Was First Collected With a Shotgun
facts.summary: Queen Alexandra's birdwing of Papua New Guinea is the largest butterfly in the world: females can span 25 to 28 centimeters (10 to 11 inches) across the wings and weigh up to 12 grams.

facts.title: Tiny Fossil Wing Scales Push Butterfly Ancestry Back 200 Million Years
facts.summary: The oldest known fossils of the insect order that includes butterflies and moths are microscopic wing scales about 200 million years old, dating from the boundary between the Triassic and Jurassic periods.
